hunks.baseline: At this very moment, that old proverb came to mind as I stared wide-eyed at the two figures approaching from far away, weaving their way between the monsters strewn across the darkness all around us.
hunks.sol: That old proverb came to mind as I stared wide-eyed at two figures approaching from far away, picking their way through the monsters strewn across the ground in the surrounding darkness.

hunks.baseline: The young man bounced along as if he had springs in his feet, while the boy beside him let out a deep, old-man-like sigh. To some people, it might have been a rather strange sight.
hunks.sol: The young man bounced along as if he had springs in the soles of his feet, while the boy beside him sighed like an old man. To some people, they might have made a strange sight.

hunks.baseline: But I—or, rather, a tiny handful of people including me—already knew who those two were.
hunks.sol: But I—or, rather, a tiny handful of people including me—already knew who they were.

hunks.baseline: Especially the young man cheerfully bouncing along in front. Even if you’d seen him only once, he had the kind of energy you could never forget.
hunks.sol: Especially the young man bouncing along in front. You could meet him only once and never forget his energy.

hunks.baseline: The name slipped from my lips before I could stop it. The people who’d been frozen in a daze after the monsters’ bizarre collapse blinked.
hunks.sol: The name slipped from my lips before I knew it. The people who’d been frozen in a daze since the monsters’ bizarre collapse blinked.

hunks.baseline: “If you mean Cheongpung, could it be…”
hunks.sol: “Cheongpung? Could it be…”

hunks.baseline: The only Cheongpung who could appear in a situation like this was someone I knew well enough to recognize at a glance. Even if you turned the whole world upside down and shook it out, there was only one.
hunks.sol: There was only one Cheongpung I knew well enough to recognize at a glance who might turn up in a situation like this. You could turn the whole world upside down and shake it out without finding another.

hunks.baseline: Of course, there were some with a reasonable question.
hunks.sol: Of course, someone raised a reasonable question.

hunks.baseline: “I can’t see from here. Captain, are you sure you’re not mistaken? Why would Young Hero Cheongpung suddenly show up here…”
hunks.sol: “I can’t see that far. Captain, are you sure you’re not mistaken? Why would Young Hero Cheongpung suddenly show up here…”

hunks.baseline: Just then, Hyuk Mujin opened his mouth, unusually cautious. A clear voice rang out from beyond the pitch-black darkness.
hunks.sol: Hyuk Mujin had barely begun speaking in an uncharacteristically cautious tone when a clear voice rang out from beyond the darkness.

hunks.baseline: “…I knew it. That voice alone is enough to make your mind go foggy. It’s definitely him.”
hunks.sol: “…Just hearing him makes my head spin. It’s definitely him.”

hunks.baseline: At this point, the voice was practically a fingerprint.
hunks.sol: At this point, that voice was practically a fingerprint.

hunks.baseline: Hyuk Mujin and I confirmed it, and then Jeok Cheongang put the matter to rest.
hunks.sol: Mujin and I had confirmed it, and Jeok Cheongang put the matter to rest.

hunks.baseline: With that final shout, Cheongpung swept in like a gust of wind, waving at me with a flushed face.
hunks.sol: With that final shout, Cheongpung swept in like a gust of wind and waved at me, his face flushed.

hunks.baseline: “I haven’t been doing well, you see. But I hoped things might be different for you, hee-hee.”
hunks.sol: “I haven’t been doing well, you see. But I hoped things might be different for you. Hee-hee.”

hunks.baseline: Watching Cheongpung cheerfully carry on even while saying something gloomy, I realized what I should do right now.
hunks.sol: Cheongpung said something gloomy as cheerfully as ever. Watching him, I realized how to respond.

hunks.baseline: More precisely, a quiet laugh slipped out of me before I knew it.
hunks.sol: Or rather, a quiet laugh escaped me before I could help it.

hunks.baseline: “Is that what you call a question? I’d laugh too if I saw the way you act, you idiot.”
hunks.sol: “You call that a question? He’s laughing because the way you act is ridiculous, you little punk.”

hunks.baseline: Swish.
hunks.sol: *Swish.*

hunks.baseline: A boy appeared from the darkness with a presence like a ghost—or rather, the greatest assassin of all time. He stared straight at me, then added:
hunks.sol: A boy appeared from the darkness, his presence as faint as a ghost’s—or rather, the greatest assassin of all time. He stared straight at me and added:

hunks.baseline: But none of us was stupid enough to sit around a campfire, chatting away, in a situation like this.
hunks.sol: But none of us was stupid enough to sit around a campfire chatting in a situation like this.

hunks.baseline: Before the warmth of our reunion had even faded, the Slaughter Saint wiped the smile from his face and got moving as if nothing had happened.
hunks.sol: Before the warmth of our reunion had faded, the Slaughter Saint wiped the smile from his face and got moving.

hunks.baseline: Jeong Hogun, the idiot the Slaughter Saint had pointed out, replied.
hunks.sol: Jeong Hogun, the idiot he’d pointed out, replied.

hunks.baseline: “I don’t know which elder you are, but you should at least show some basic courtesy. I am a Thousand Captain of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, serving under His Majesty the Emperor’s solemn command…”
hunks.sol: “I don’t know what sort of elder you are, but you should at least show some courtesy. I am a Thousand Captain of the Embroidered Uniform Guard, serving under His Majesty the Emperor’s solemn command…”

hunks.baseline: The Slaughter Saint’s figure blurred.

hunks.baseline: Then came the sound of wind, and a gleaming blue dagger pressed against Jeong Hogun’s neck.
hunks.sol: The Slaughter Saint’s figure blurred. Wind swept past, and a gleaming blue dagger came to rest against Jeong Hogun’s neck.

hunks.baseline: “Keep talking. If you waste even a few more moments, I’ll make you a real dead man.”
hunks.sol: “Go on. Keep talking. Waste even a few more moments and I’ll make you a *late* elder.”

hunks.baseline: Everyone, myself included, recognized the loyalty Jeong Hogun and his Embroidered Uniform Guards had for the Emperor. It was extraordinary.
hunks.sol: Everyone, myself included, recognized the extraordinary loyalty Jeong Hogun and his Embroidered Uniform Guards bore the Emperor.

hunks.baseline: Unlike the Emperor, who was somewhere far away, the dagger was right in front of him. Jeong Hogun stared at it in silence before finally speaking with a grim face.
hunks.sol: The Emperor was somewhere far away. The dagger was right against Jeong Hogun’s neck. He stared at it for a moment, then spoke with a grim face.

hunks.baseline: The Slaughter Saint replied in a dry voice to what was an exceedingly poor excuse for an Embroidered Uniform Guard.
hunks.sol: It was an embarrassingly poor excuse for an Embroidered Uniform Guard. The Slaughter Saint replied dryly.

hunks.baseline: “Of course we know each other, but I said we’re not close.”
hunks.sol: “Of course we know each other. I said we’re not close.”

hunks.baseline: The Slaughter Saint had spared him the last shred of his dignity in the name of martial-world etiquette. By the time he lowered the dagger, most of our three thousand allies were staring at him in shock.
hunks.sol: The Slaughter Saint had let him keep that last scrap of dignity in the name of martial-world etiquette. By the time he put away the dagger, most of our three thousand allies were staring at him in shock.

hunks.baseline: A boy who wasn’t even twenty, no matter how generously you counted, had subdued a Thousand Captain of the Embroidered Uniform Guard who stood at the very peak of the Peak realm.
hunks.sol: A boy who couldn’t be twenty, even by the most generous estimate, had subdued a Thousand Captain of the Embroidered Uniform Guard who had reached the far end of the Peak realm.

hunks.baseline: And he’d done it in one swift move, so fast he’d been impossible to see.
hunks.sol: In a single move, so fast no one could see it.

hunks.baseline: Everyone was astonished by the unbelievable sight before them, but Perfected Being Hyeoncheon seemed more shaken than anyone.
hunks.sol: Everyone was astonished, but Perfected Being Hyeoncheon seemed more shaken than anyone.

hunks.baseline: The view changes depending on where you stand.
hunks.sol: What you can see depends on where you stand.

hunks.baseline: Perfected Being Hyeoncheon was a seasoned Supreme Peak master, skilled enough to vaguely discern the Slaughter Saint’s true realm. He was so caught up in shock and confusion that he couldn’t continue. Bow Saint spoke for him.
hunks.sol: Perfected Being Hyeoncheon was a seasoned Supreme Peak master, skilled enough to make out something of the Slaughter Saint’s true realm. Shock and confusion left him unable to say more, and Bow Saint spoke in his place.

hunks.baseline: The Slaughter Saint had seen through her identity, just as she had his. He answered with a bitter smile.
hunks.sol: The Slaughter Saint had recognized her, just as she had recognized him. He answered with a bitter smile.

hunks.baseline: “I feel the same. I thought we’d never meet again after that day.”
hunks.sol: “I feel the same. After that day, I thought we’d never meet again.”

hunks.baseline: As the people around them grew more confused with every word they exchanged, Bow Saint quietly added:
hunks.sol: The people around them looked more confused with every word they exchanged. Bow Saint quietly added:

hunks.baseline: The air around us seemed to crackle.
hunks.sol: For an instant, the air seemed to crackle.

hunks.baseline: Once condemned by the whole martial world, he had become the greatest assassin of all time after the Great War between the Orthodox and Demonic factions began, striking fear into countless great fiends.
hunks.sol: Once condemned by the whole martial world, he had gone on to strike fear into countless great fiends after the Great War between the Orthodox and Demonic factions began. He was the greatest assassin of all time.

hunks.baseline: Those two words alone were enough to explain the situation and make everyone understand.
hunks.sol: Those two words were enough to explain the situation to everyone.

hunks.baseline: Of course, there wasn’t.
hunks.sol: Of course there wasn’t.

hunks.baseline: Or, to be precise, even if there was, there shouldn’t be.
hunks.sol: Or, to be precise, even if there was, there had better not be.

hunks.baseline: Not if the person asking was called the Slaughter Saint.
hunks.sol: Not when the person asking was the Slaughter Saint.

hunks.baseline: Jeong Hogun and the other Embroidered Uniform Guards began throwing off their armor with the speed of reservists who’d just finished a training exercise and were hurrying home. The Slaughter Saint’s eyes suddenly narrowed.
hunks.sol: Jeong Hogun and the other Embroidered Uniform Guards threw off their armor with the speed of reservists heading home after training. The Slaughter Saint’s eyes suddenly narrowed.

hunks.baseline: I also understood why he’d called a perfectly healthy human being a thing.
hunks.sol: I also understood why he’d called a human being with all his limbs intact a *thing*.

hunks.baseline: “Well, how should I put it… That gentleman’s a little out of his mind.”
hunks.sol: “Well, how should I put it… That gentleman’s mind wanders a bit.”

hunks.baseline: “…I’ve already gathered that.”
hunks.sol: “…I’ve gathered that much.”

hunks.baseline: The Slaughter Saint sighed as he watched the Great Sir, who had somehow blended in among the Embroidered Uniform Guards and was cheerfully stripping off his clothes.
hunks.sol: The Slaughter Saint sighed as he watched Great Sir, who had somehow blended in among the Embroidered Uniform Guards and was enthusiastically stripping off his clothes.

hunks.baseline: The original madman, of course, was watching the new madman’s striptease in wonder.
hunks.sol: The original madman, of course, was watching the newcomer’s display of physical beauty from right beside him, full of admiration.

hunks.baseline: The Great Sir, whom Jeong Hogun had just stopped from removing his underwear, noticed Cheongpung and brightened.
hunks.sol: Jeong Hogun stopped Great Sir just as he was about to remove his underwear. Great Sir spotted Cheongpung, and his eyes lit up.

hunks.baseline: “You’re a spirited young man. I like that. I’m Soonja.”
hunks.sol: “You’re a spirited young man. Good to see. I’m Soonja.”

hunks.baseline: Just as everyone stood aghast at the meeting of two natural disasters that shouldn’t occur even once in a hundred years, the Slaughter Saint shook his head and spoke.
hunks.sol: Everyone stood aghast at the meeting of two natural disasters that shouldn’t occur even once in a hundred years. The Slaughter Saint shook his head.

hunks.baseline: Or maybe it would be more accurate to say that they did, and they didn’t.
hunks.sol: Or maybe it would be more accurate to say they did, but their pursuit never reached us.

hunks.baseline: The Slaughter Saint said that and left us several times. Each time he returned just when we needed him, his body reeking of blood.
hunks.sol: The Slaughter Saint left us several times with those words. Each time, he returned just when he needed to, reeking of blood.

hunks.baseline: After nearly two full days had passed, he said, “It should be less of a nuisance from here on.”
hunks.sol: After nearly two full days, he said, “They should be less of a nuisance from here on.”

hunks.baseline: Not one of our three thousand allies, myself included, doubted what he meant: he’d shaken off Dark Heaven’s relentless pursuit.
hunks.sol: Not one of our three thousand allies, myself included, failed to understand what he meant. He’d shaken off Dark Heaven’s relentless pursuit.

hunks.baseline: And we all knew how he’d dealt with the pursuers so quickly—and that it was he and Cheongpung, not the Great Sir, who had taken down the ten thousand monsters.
hunks.sol: We understood, too, that he’d made quick work of the pursuers—and that he and Cheongpung, not Great Sir, were the reason ten thousand monsters had fallen.

hunks.baseline: “Mm! Mm!”
hunks.sol: “Mmph, mmph.”

hunks.baseline: The trophy—no, the black-robed man bound from head to toe in rope—twitched. Taishan, who was running with him tucked under one arm like a piece of luggage, raised a fist as big as a cauldron lid.
hunks.sol: The war trophy—no, the black-robed man bound from head to toe in rope—wriggled. Taishan, who was running with him tucked under one arm like a piece of luggage, raised a fist as big as a cauldron lid.

hunks.baseline: “Mm! Mmm!”
hunks.sol: “Mmph. Mmmph!”

hunks.baseline: The black-robed man immediately fell silent as a mouse. Our allies had been on a brutal forced march for days without rest, but before long we finally escaped that miserable wilderness.
hunks.sol: The black-robed man went still and silent as a mouse. Our allies had been on a brutal forced march for days without rest, but before long we finally left that miserable wilderness behind.

hunks.baseline: What awaited us was an enormous lake I’d never seen before, and a group of beggars huddled around it, lighting campfires.
hunks.sol: Waiting for us was an enormous lake unlike any I’d ever seen. Around it, a group of beggars huddled together beside their campfires.

hunks.baseline: One of them had a face we knew very well.
hunks.sol: Among them was a very familiar face.

hunks.baseline: A face so shabby you’d reach for your wallet just by looking at it from a distance.
hunks.sol: A face so shabby it made you reach for your wallet even from a distance.
